_comment: Instance-recognition registry for the SNIP-CONTRACT 'Fragment boundary' rule. A named child instance may be selected independently when its parent serves only as context for that child instance; sibling instances and context-parent statements are then outside the selected fragment. Whether a child block is such an instance is grammar knowledge, not tree shape — a named rib-group and a policy 'term' are structurally identical. This file is parser/validation knowledge ONLY. It is not a service taxonomy and carries no naming, category, or relationship meaning.
_stability: Versioned and frozen for the duration of a Count/_bindings generation. Any change to instanceKeywords, bareNameContainers, contextLeafPaths, or notSelectable MUST trigger a full 'Seen on' re-audit and regeneration of Count and _bindings for every affected JVD, because a registry change can change which devices a body reproduces on.
_contextLeafPaths: Exact root-to-leaf keyword paths whose ancestors provide context when the template selects only that leaf below them. This does not admit partial ports, tunnel-services blocks, or similarly named containers elsewhere.
_instanceKeywords: A child block is an instance of its container when its header has a leading grammar keyword listed here followed by a name or index (e.g. 'unit 0', 'neighbor 10.0.0.1').
_bareNameContainers: Containers whose children are named solely by an identifier, with no leading grammar keyword (e.g. 'rib-groups { RG-REMOTE-LOOPBACKS { ... } }'). A single-token child block inside one of these containers is an instance.
_notSelectable: Explicitly recorded non-instances. These read as named child blocks but are ordered constituents of the stanza that encloses them: their neighbours change the meaning of the selection, so an unselected sibling invalidates the claim.

notSelectable.term: A policy-statement term is an ordered constituent. A device carrying an extra term (for example EVPN-T5-ONLY) evaluates differently and MUST NOT match a snip that selects only some terms.
